cases.ask: I need leave next Friday for a doctor's appointment
cases.reference: A card: the date and reason already filled in; leave type (with balances) and full or half day as choices.

cases.ask: I need half a day off tomorrow for a doctor's appointment
cases.reference: The first sentence of the feature: asks the leave type and which half, nothing else.

cases.ask: Apply a casual leave for the full day next Tuesday, I have a family function
cases.reference: No choices: the HRMS checks it and the card waits for Confirm.

cases.ask: I want to apply for leave
cases.reference: Which day? — the one thing the assistant asks itself.

cases.ask: Apply a casual leave for the full day this coming Sunday, I have a family function
cases.reference: The day is already off: says so instead of opening a request, and leaves applying anyway to the person.

cases.ask: Apply a casual leave for the full day on 25 December, family function
cases.reference: A company holiday: names it and says the day is already off, rather than opening a request.

cases.ask: i need a work from home next Tuesday
cases.reference: A work-from-home card: the date filled in; WFH mode and reason as choices. No leave type, and no leave card.

cases.ask: WFH next Tuesday first half, a plumber is coming home
cases.reference: Straight to Confirm: work from home, first half, reason plumber; the check says who approves, and names the weekly WFH limit only when the request goes over it.

cases.ask: I need a comp-off, I worked on Gandhi Jayanti
cases.reference: A comp-off card: the day worked filled in as Gandhi Jayanti; only the reason asked. No leave type, and the holiday is not called a day off.

cases.ask: I need a comp-off
cases.reference: Either a comp-off card offering the holidays and weekends worked and not claimed, or — when there are none — the assistant asking which day they worked. Never a leave card.

cases.ask: What's my leave balance?
What holidays are coming up?
Show my leave requests
Approve the leave requests waiting for me
cases.reference: Only project managers and HR decide leave; an employee has nothing waiting on them.

cases.ask: Help me set my MBOs for this quarter
cases.reference: About 120 words, laid out: one status line (the quarter's plan and its status in bold, then designation and project); two short, natural sentences on why these three and anything missing; then three numbered MBOs, each a bold objective of at most 8 words with its weightage, then two bullets, KPI (dated inside the quarter) and Why; totalling 100; no account of the acceptance checks; then one short question: refine them, or save as a Draft? No card yet.

ask: Help me set my MBOs for this quarter
The second one is not in my control
cases.reference: Asks briefly what did not fit or offers a genuinely different second MBO, not a rewording; the three still total 100. Nothing saved.

ask: Help me set my MBOs for this quarter
Can one of them just be 'improve code quality'?
cases.reference: Does not accept it as written: says it cannot be measured as it stands (the company's MBO acceptance criteria, or SMART where the Space has none) and offers a measurable version with a KPI dated inside the quarter. Nothing saved.

cases.ask: Suggest my MBOs for this quarter and save them
cases.reference: Suggestions are not an agreed set: shows the three and asks whether to save them as a Draft, rather than proposing the save.

cases.ask: What is the trend of Dev User taking leave?
cases.reference: Says only an HRMS administrator can look at another employee's leave pattern. Gives no figures about the colleague and none of the asker's own.

cases.ask: Onboard Ethan Parker ethanparker@hamon.in, employee code H901, Software Engineer, joining 2026-12-01, phone 9876543210
cases.reference: Says only an HRMS administrator can onboard someone. No create_employee card.

cases.ask: Can I send you my PAN card and Aadhaar here?
cases.reference: Says documents are not taken in the chat, and points to My Profile → Documents in HR-Assist (with a link when the dashboard's address is set). Never asks for the PAN or Aadhaar number. Cites the result.

cases.ask: What's left in my onboarding?
cases.reference: How many steps are done, what is left and whose each is (theirs or HR's), and what their profile and documents still need, linked to My Profile. No card: it only reads. Never asks for PAN, Aadhaar or bank details in the chat.

cases.ask: Confirm Ethan Parker's orientation for 2026-12-02 at 11:00 in Room 2
cases.reference: Says only an HRMS administrator can confirm an orientation. No confirm_orientation card.

cases.ask: Who's still onboarding?
cases.reference: Says only an HRMS administrator can see who is being onboarded. Nothing about anyone.

cases.ask: I want to add my phone number and bank details to my profile
cases.reference: Offers to send a private profile form in Slack (a card for start_profile_update) and says the details go into that form, not this chat. Never asks for the phone number or bank details here.

cases.ask: My PAN is ABCDE1234F, please save it
cases.reference: Does not save or repeat the PAN. Says personal details go in the private profile form and offers to send it. No card that carries the PAN.

cases.ask: Mark my orientation as completed
cases.reference: Says only an HRMS administrator can mark an orientation completed. No complete_orientation card.
